what: the second fix round (every kind of fact gets a check) and the freeze of version 3.2 at nine languages

digest.part: Stage 3a-fix2 (the second fix round: every kind of fact gets a check) and the freeze of version 3.2 at nine ported languages (ts go py c zig clojure rust elixir rb). Records read: brief.md, brief5.md, results/s3fix2-guard.txt, results/s3fix2-shared.txt, results/s3fix2-tools.txt, results/s3fix2-final.txt. All were present and read completely.

rounds.purpose: Answer the independent re-check of v3.1, which judged it not ready for three reasons. (1) A wrong fact in the `language` or `convention` category hides behind the mask, and shared code supplies a runtime value by an undeclared default (`lit(r, false)` in ReadmeRef.ts:78). (2) The runtime reader cannot see throws, static or class receivers, fields, lua's error value, or real stream timing. (3) A dropped sentence leaves no trace in a new port. The stage's rule: every printed fact is checked by someone other than its writer, and the kind of check follows from the kind of fact (derived, cited code token, cited absence, cited prose, language or convention, sentence).
rounds.who: Three engineers in parallel on disjoint files: i-shared (shared doc code and providers), i-guard (guard, reader, forms, runtime-table), i-tools (review tools). A fourth, v32, merges the three, reviews, freezes v3.2 and writes PORTING.md 3.2.
rounds.produced: The task split and the fact-kind/check table.
rounds.changed: Set the rules: shared code never supplies a runtime value by default; the reader must see every dimension a page states; `language` holds only what no runtime file can show, so null and boolean literals become cited.

rounds.purpose: Make the reader and the guard see failure markers, receivers, field-or-callable, comment-read returns, optional parameters, absent member families and stream timing. Move none and lits from `language` to cited. Add absence citations and stricter citation rules. Audit every citation.
rounds.who: One builder, working on test-side files only (29 commits on 9089ed48, HEAD 41a6df87). Checks were the builder's own: guard plus reader, the suite, the 75 earlier mutations re-run and 19 new mutations.
rounds.produced: Reader and table dimensions for all 20 runtimes. runtime-table.md grew from 872 to 1108 lines. A 129-row citation audit. Stream records for all 20. Table corrections for swift, lua, ocaml, perl, java, kotlin, scala, cpp and c. Five WRONG facts in three ported languages.
rounds.changed: Found that clojure and elixir declare streamLazy but read every item before returning; that the swift stream fits no kind; and that c's page omits sdk_options_map and sdk_get_utility. All were recorded as WRONG or NEEDS SHARED and left to the shared engineer. 3 breaking forms-framework changes and 5 additive.

rounds.purpose: Remove every runtime value that shared code supplied by default, fix the stream sentences, decide the checked-example rule by result style, correct false notes, and fix the rb data/options sentence.
rounds.who: One builder (4 commits, HEAD 51de033a). Checks were the builder's own: build, suite, golden, seven lanes, the unported diff and the portcheck per language.
rounds.produced: A defaults sweep of 45 rows. Ten defaults became facts and six fallbacks now throw. New required facts: direct.okFalse, accessor.param, Member.runs, setArg, pairForm/noError, abortCode. The checked-example rule by result style. Elixir's arity claims removed.
rounds.changed: 8 breaking interface changes; 'as they arrive' was dropped from the stream sentences as false for every runtime. The suite was left with 9 failures, the guard's account tests, which needed the guard engineer's files.

rounds.purpose: Compare language and convention facts with the OLD page, flag dropped sentences (including from scratch), export the sentences nobody read, carry out smaller fixes, and measure H1 prose by source.
rounds.who: One builder, working on the tools only, with no sdkgen source changed. The check was the builder's own self-test: 176 controls, 0 failed.
rounds.produced: Fact attestation, with UNATTESTED failing portcheck. A 'printed less often than its reference' check and a non-failing absent list. A from-scratch mode for every control. sentences.js with 288 distinct masked sentences, 234 of them resting only on rule records. A by-source prose measure.
rounds.changed: Made the brief's attestation rule per context, because the brief's 'at least one unit' rule let clojure entityNoun 'Fields' through. Fixed the duplicate check, which was hiding a from-scratch hole (sentence-removed-go). Left the nine checks at 2 PASS and 7 FAIL, on 16 unattested facts.

rounds.purpose: Merge the three engineers' work, settle where they disagree, review the nine languages where output changed, freeze v3.2 and write PORTING.md 3.2.
rounds.who: One engineer (v32), who did not build the three parts. 68 commits on 9089ed48, tag v32-frozen = 3d58cb46, tools git d2e3b26. Checks: the full freeze set, mutations (75 + 19 + 12 new), end-to-end runs of the re-check's provider mutations, an injection from scratch, and newport.sh on kotlin.
rounds.produced: v3.2 frozen in P/base32. PORTING.md has 621 lines, runtime-table.md 1119. The nine one-command checks pass. Self-test: 175 controls, 0 failed. Measures recorded for H1, H2, H3 and H4.
rounds.changed: `runs` and accessor.param are derived by the guard; okFalse, abortCode and noError are cited, with ahead okFalse citations in all 11 unported forms. c documents options and utility. The copy claims now rest on a cited copy fact. The STREAM_RUNS.call sentence was corrected. The test sentence names its arguments by position. okFalse throws when missing. Five stale hand records were re-decided and 7 unattested facts recorded by hand. Disagreements resolved or deferred (ocaml).

findings.finding: Version 3.2 is frozen at nine languages (tag v32-frozen, 3d58cb46), and every freeze check holds there. The suite has 2597 tests with 0 failing, guard plus reader pass 61/61, the golden passes 2/2, and all seven documentation lanes that can run here pass. The nine one-command checks pass with 0 open and 0 unattested facts, and the tools self-test passes 175/175.

The interface did not settle. Breaking provider-interface changes since the first four languages now total about 20 to 22 against H1's line of about 10, crossed about twice over. None came from a newly ported language: each turned a value that shared code had silently supplied into a declared fact. The eleven remaining ports will show whether it has stopped moving.

H2 is refuted wherever the checking machinery is counted. For the nine languages, documentation code alone is 1.61x smaller, 1.33x with the forms files and 0.98x with the shared guard. Projected to twenty, only documentation code at x1 provider size (2.26x) stays above the 2x line.

Prose that providers write themselves is small: at most 7.4% by source (go, mostly its stream note), under H1's 15% line. Counted as 'printed by this language alone', go is 22.6%, over the line, though most of that is shared code that only go's result style selects.

Making facts explicit found real false statements that the earlier checks had passed. clojure and elixir claimed lazy streams that read every item first. c's page omitted two real client members. elixir's arity notes were false. And 'as they arrive' was false for every runtime, because every streaming feature yields from a response already read whole.

Shared defaults were hiding defects. Making fallbacks throw broke clojure's REFERENCE at once, because its signatures had never been parsed. c, zig and go had printed defaults that were true only by luck. A required fact also needs a runtime throw: with okFalse bypassed, the page would have printed `undefined`.

The checks now catch the re-check's attacks end to end. Wrong rb `none` and okFalse fail the guard; wrong `maps` and `noun` fail the one command in both modes; a sentence dropped from one variation leaves an open class from scratch. Mutations: 68 of v3.1's 75, 17 of the guard engineer's 19 and 11 of the 12 new ones are caught. The rest are known and accounted, and one (py okFalse removed) fails the build.

Several checks rest on people rather than mechanism. 229 of 297 shared sentences rest only on stage-3a rule records nobody re-read, and no sentence has a verdict. 67 citations are pinned prose that only a reviewer checks. Hand records are pinned by count, and five had gone stale unseen.

H4 holds for what can run here: ts, go, py, c, rust, rb and zig documentation lanes all pass at the freeze, including c's new checked examples. clojure and elixir changed blocks are compiled by nothing, because no compiler is present.

Within one stream kind, runtimes differ in when the operation runs, so a separate `runs` fact was needed, and it is now derived by the guard. The two engineers agreed on its value for all 20 runtimes. The change also exposed that the shared 'call' sentence was false for java, kotlin, scala and perl, which none of the nine ported languages exercises.

Some gaps remain open. Portcheck does not notice a stale build and printed PASS after a failed build. ReadmeRefFeatures still prints TypeScript-shaped `active: false` for all twenty languages. The ocaml stream kind is left for its porter. H3 was not re-measured against the 329-issue catalogue and H5 was not exercised.

Each language must now supply more: a forms file of 54 to 113 lines, a test-constructor name, a 7-line stream record, receiver and failure markers where the defaults do not fit, and none, okFalse and absence citations. The guard and forms framework had 3 breaking changes from the guard engineer plus 1 from the v32 engineer, each forcing edits in existing forms files.
